page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 96 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in compute-heavy tasks. The processor features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier performance in image and text processing, as well as strong results in ray tracing and software compilation. Single-threaded and multi-threaded decompression benchmarks, such as bzip3, fall into the top 25% tier. For machine learning workloads, the hardware delivers strong prompt processing speeds for small and medium LLM models, and top-tier text generation speeds for small models.

Given its high vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the c4n-highcpu-48 offers high compute density. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring raw CPU throughput and vector or matrix acceleration without the overhead of large memory footprints or local storage. This makes it highly suitable for workloads such as software compilation, image and text processing pipelines, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 96 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor. With a resource ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core, this instance is designed for high-throughput compute tasks rather than memory-intensive applications. It contains no local storage or integrated GPUs. Benchmark data highlights strong performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and cryptography, alongside top-tier results in image and text processing. The processor's support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions enables efficient execution of vector calculations and small-to-medium machine learning inference. This instance is well-suited for CPU-bound workloads, including web serving, data compression, and text processing pipelines.
